newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Great Eagle FY96 results best expectation.
newsitem.headline: Great Eagle FY96 results best expectation.

text.p: Great Eagle Holdings Ltd's full year results were slightly above expectations, and while the next couple of years are likely to be tougher, analysts said they are maintaining their favourable recommendations for the stock.
"The results were actually quite good, although they are boosted by exceptional gains," said Adrian Ngan, senior property analyst at Peregrine Securities.
Great Eagle reported net profit of HK$1.06 billion for the year ended September 30, an increase of 28.7 percent and slightly above the consensus forecast of HK$1.01 billion.
The bottom line was boosted by exceptional gains of HK$396.73 million derived from the sale of four floors of the group's showcase office tower Citibank Plaza in March 1996.
"We would have seen good growth in rental income were it not for the sale of those four floors," said Ngan. "But as a result (of the sale) it was a bit sluggish."
Operating profit before exceptional items rose to HK$892.99 million, up from HK$726.71 million. The results also included the operating profit of the group's growing hotel division.
Analysts said that the company was still attractive because it was trading at a large discount to estimated net asset value of HK$48.00 to HK$50,00 per share.
Great Eagle closed HK$0.90 higher at HK$34.00 on Wednesday.
But they added the property investment and hotel owning group was likely to face low and negative earnings growth in the coming two years.
"Rental reversions will be very flat this year," said Ngan, referring to increases in rental rates derived from the renewal of tenant's lease contracts and from new contracts.
He said leases were signed or renewed in 1994 and 1995 at high rates and that rents had eased slightly in 1996.
"With the spin-off of its commercial property arm, Great Eagle itself will not be so interesting," said one analyst with an overseas brokerage.
The company said in a statement in August 1996 that it was planning a reorganisation, which would ultimately result in the separate listing of its investment property division.
The overseas analyst also said he was forecasting a dip in earnings in 1998.
"We are not forecasting any exceptional items for that period and unless the Mongkok project is completed early, which is unlikely, there will be little to boost earnings," the overseas analyst said.

The company's joint venture urban renewal project with the government's Land Development Corp (LDC) to redevelop a large plot in the densely populated Mongkok district in the heart of Kowloon received approval from the government for compulsory resumption of the remaining unacquired properties, the company said in its results announcement.
The Mongkok project is scheduled to be completed in 2000.
